classification.difficultyReason: Interpret internal and external circle tangencies as differences and sums of radii, then recognise the right triangle of centres and solve the scaffolded radius equation.

content.prompt: The diagram shows the logo of a particular company. The large circle has centre $O$ and radius $12\text{ cm}$ and $AB$ is a diameter. $D$ is the centre of the middle-sized circle with diameter $OB$. Finally, $C$ is the centre of the smallest circle.

spec.description: Five unshaded tangent circles with a dashed horizontal diameter and marked centres O, C and D. No OC or DC construction segments are supplied. Ordinary source blue/red marks use black.
spec.mathematics: Outer radius 12; middle-circle radii 6; two congruent smaller circles tangent internally to the outer circle and externally to both middle circles. Drawing coordinates establish exact tangency without printing the unknown radius.
spec.answerVisibility: No unknown radius or requested length is labelled.

sizing.exceptionReason: Five tangent circles and five required labels need readable clearance at the tangencies.

children.label: a
children.prompt: What is the radius of the circle with centre $D$?

answer.worked: Its diameter is $OB=12\text{ cm}$, so its radius is $12\div2=6\text{ cm}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the radius of the circle with centre $C$ is $r\text{ cm}$, express these in terms of $r$.

answer.worked: The smaller circle touches the large circle internally, so the distance between their centres is the difference of their radii: $OC=(12-r)\text{ cm}$.
The circles with centres $D$ and $C$ touch externally, so the distance between their centres is the sum of their radii: $DC=(6+r)\text{ cm}$.

answer.short:
$r=4$

Apply Pythagoras to the right triangle of centres $OCD$.
answer.worked:
By symmetry, $OC$ is perpendicular to the diameter $AB$. In right triangle $OCD$, $OD=6\text{ cm}$, $OC=(12-r)\text{ cm}$ and $DC=(6+r)\text{ cm}$.
$$\begin{align*}DC^2&=OD^2+OC^2\\(6+r)^2&=6^2+(12-r)^2\\36+12r+r^2&=36+144-24r+r^2\\36+12r&=180-24r\\36r&=144\\r&=4\end{align*}$$
The smallest circle has radius $4\text{ cm}$.
